schema.description: One place a phone stayed: a run of consecutive place.track fixes that held within a small radius for a while, with its centroid and, when a geocoder could name it, the place. Derived by the stays importer (source osm) from the same spool the owntracks importer reads, never by changing a place.track fact. The identity is the device and the stay's start instant; a stay still open is re-emitted whole as it grows and when it closes, so a resend replaces it. The place is optional: a stay with no geocode yet is still the fact that the phone was here then, and the place backfills on a later run. start is the fact time. Version 2 requires source_time, every other rule unchanged. Version 3 only rewords this description.

id.description: "stay:", the device and the start instant. The identity: one facet per phone per stay.

device.description: The phone the fixes came from, as OwnTracks named it.

start.description: The fix time of the first fix in the stay, a UTC instant. The fact time.

end.description: The fix time of the last fix in the stay so far, a UTC instant. Equal to or after start; moves later while the stay is open.

lat.description: The stay's centroid latitude in degrees, WGS-84: the mean of its fixes.

lon.description: The stay's centroid longitude in degrees, WGS-84: the mean of its fixes.

fixes.description: How many fixes the stay holds.

radius_m.description: How far the stay spreads: the greatest distance in metres from the centroid to any of its fixes.

place.description: What a geocoder made of the centroid. Absent until one could name it.

name.description: A readable name built from the address: the most specific of suburb, village, hamlet or town, then city or county, then state, then country. The display_name when none of those are known.
examples: Al Garhoud, Dubai, United Arab Emirates

display_name.description: The geocoder's own full label for the point.
examples: Dubai International Airport, Al Garhoud, Dubai, United Arab Emirates

osm_type.description: The OSM element kind the point resolved to: node, way or relation.

osm_id.description: The OSM element id, so the answer can be traced back to the source.

address.description: The geocoder's address parts, as it returned them: open-ended keys, each a string. strict mode needs the value schema set.

geocoder.description: The source of the name, so a reader knows whose guess this is.

geocoded_at.description: When the geocoder was asked, a UTC instant: the name is only as current as this.

source_time.description: How the phone's clock was read: value is the first fix's tst, the epoch OwnTracks writes in UTC by its definition, as its digits (basis source).

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.
